note:
The YOUNGER SELFIE variant of the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research - templates/page.research-argireline.json, section `key_findings`, blocks f1, f2, f3. Malcolm, 2026-08-26: new models, aged thirty to forty, amateur, and make the pictures CLEARLY selfies. All earlier waves kept.

MALCOLM, 2026-08-26 - TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PREVIOUS 40s WAVE, AND THE FIRST ONE IS A CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF.

1. NO HAND, NO ARM, NO PHONE - AND THE REASONING MATTERS. The previous wave REQUIRED a raised arm cutting into the bottom corner as the strongest selfie tell. That was wrong: this is the view THROUGH the front camera of the phone she is holding, so the hand holding it physically cannot appear in its own frame, and neither can the phone. Asking for a raised arm also gave the engines licence to escalate to a visible hand and handset, which several did - nbp_pro put a phone in frame four separate times across these waves. So limbs are barred outright, in the prompt body and in the negatives, and the selfie read is carried entirely by the CAMERA instead: a close wide lens exaggerating the nose and chin, an angle that is deliberately not eye level, a gaze on the screen rather than the lens, a crooked and off-centre frame, phone-file noise and wrong indoor white balance, and a lived-in room. Those tells are all true of a real selfie; a visible holding hand is not.

2. NO BAKED-IN TEXT OF ANY KIND, BECAUSE THE STORE IS MULTILINGUAL. The percentage, the BEFORE / AFTER caption and the qualifier line must NOT be part of the image. Skingenetix runs nine languages through Langify, which translates page content but cannot touch pixels - a figure burned into a JPEG is permanently English. The labels therefore go on in the THEME as translatable HTML over the image, and the asset itself ships clean. scripts/label-before-after.py is from here on a PREVIEW tool for judging candidates, not a publishing step, and contact sheets for this wave are built WITHOUT labels so what is judged is what would actually ship. This also removes the last reason to fear engine-drawn lettering on the plate area - but the no-text negatives stay, because a garbled word anywhere in frame is still fatal.

WHY FORTY TO FIFTY, AND WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER TO A TRADE-OFF MALCOLM WAS SHOWN. He first asked for thirty to forty; the flag raised before that wave ran was that a woman of thirty-eight has fine, early lines, so half the depth of an already-shallow line is a much smaller visible difference - which fights his earlier instruction that the percentage improvement must actually be SEEN. He moved the casting to forty to fifty on that basis. This band is the useful middle: the lines are ESTABLISHED and hold a real shadow, so a half-depth change is legible, while the woman is still plausibly a customer rather than a case study. The thirty-to-forty wave was already part generated and was allowed to finish, so both bands exist side by side and the difference can be judged rather than argued.

THE AGE BAND CUTS BOTH WAYS AND BOTH ARE NEGATED. Left alone, the engines reach for deep wrinkles because the brief is about wrinkles - producing a sixty-year-old. Pushed too hard the other way they produce an unlined thirty-year-old and there is nothing to show. So the brief states the lines are established but not the deep folds of a woman in her sixties, that a few greys at the parting are right and a full head of grey is not, and the negatives name a woman over fifty-five and a woman under forty. CHECK AGE PLAUSIBILITY FIRST ON EVERY CANDIDATE.

CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED:
  * THE HONESTY DEVICE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels, NO LINE MAY DISAPPEAR, only depth changes. Session variance applies to the PHOTOGRAPH, never to the FINDING.
  * ITS SELFIE EXTENSION: she must not come back better GROOMED. Each after-panel names what must survive - freckles, acne marks and under-eye shadows on f1; dry patches, broken capillaries and chapped lips on f2; active blemishes, oily skin and thick brows on f3.
  * NO CAPTION-SHAPED NOUNS. nbp_pro drew "FIRST VISIT"/"FOLLOW-UP" in r3, seedream drew "VISIT" in the full-face wave, and nbp_pro put text along the bottom edge again in selfie r2 even with the word removed entirely. The word appears nowhere here - verified by count before running - but nbp_pro reaches for captions on this brief regardless of wording, so check the frame edges on all of its candidates.
  * THREE NEW WOMEN, none used in any previous wave.
  * SKIN REALISM SPECIFIED POSITIVELY - pore size varying by zone, asymmetric never-mirrored pigmentation, vellus hair, greasy-to-dry variation. Sheen, glow, dewy and hydrated stay banned; they render as speckled white highlights reading as dry flaking.

KNOWN SUPPLIER STATE AT TIME OF WRITING: the Gemini pair is working again - Malcolm cleared the billing spending cap that returned HTTP 429 across the earlier selfie waves, verified by direct probe on both models. Luma refuses this brief family with HTTP 422 (five occurrences) because it has no negative-prompt field and the negative list folds into its prompt body; expect it to be absent. flux2 returns one candidate per call regardless of the flag and has twice produced watermark-like marks here, so check its frames at full size.

⚠️ NOTE ON CANDIDATE COUNT: generate-multi.py reads candidates from its --candidates CLI flag ONLY and ignores any `candidates` key in this config. A previous wave set 4 here and silently got 2. Pass it on the command line.

⚠️ PALETTE: a selfie cannot carry Acetyl's Pearl grey D8D6D4 studio ground without destroying the premise, so these blocks would lose the page's scene colour.
⚠️ SITE OF MEASUREMENT: all three trials measured the PERIORBITAL region, so a full-face frame shows more than the site measured. Block copy and alt text must not imply otherwise.
⚠️ RENDER SIZE: 660px desktop / 350px mobile split in two, so each face renders about 330px / 175px. Combined with the younger casting, the change may not survive the downscale. Judge at render size before choosing.

CLASS B, no references. Square 2048x2048, each panel a 1:2 portrait.

slots.title: f1 · Wang 2013 — 48.9% anti-wrinkle efficacy vs 0% placebo, 4 weeks  —  selfie 40s r2
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary phone selfies of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier one, the right panel is the later one.

HER WHOLE FACE IS IN VIEW IN BOTH PANELS - head and shoulders, the entire face from above the hairline to the collarbones, nothing cropped off. Both eyes, the nose, the whole mouth and the full jawline are visible. Her expression is flat and unposed on both days, mouth closed, not smiling.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and cut, and her permanent marks - moles, freckles, blemish marks - in the same places on her face.

CLEARLY DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO OCCASIONS:
  * PLACE AND LIGHT - on the earlier day she is in a bedroom in the evening with only the ceiling light on, a flat yellowish light straight down that puts shadow under her eyes; on the later day she is sitting by a window in flat grey afternoon daylight, much cooler and softer, with the curtain edge behind her. The two pictures plainly were not taken in the same room or the same conditions.
  * CAMERA ANGLE - she holds the phone differently each time, so it sits at a different height and to a different side of her face, and the wide-lens distortion falls differently as a result.
  * EYE GAZE - her eyes go to a different part of the screen each time.
  * BACKGROUND - a completely different part of an ordinary home, at a different brightness.
  * CLOTHES - a completely different everyday garment, a different colour and neckline.
  * HAIR - the same cut, unstyled, falling differently: a different parting, flatter on one day, flyaway strands out of place.

She must never stop being recognisably the same woman, and she must not appear older or younger, heavier or thinner, in one panel than the other.

IT MUST BE OBVIOUS AT A GLANCE THAT SHE TOOK THIS HERSELF - BUT THE PHONE AND HER HANDS ARE NEVER IN THE PICTURE. This is the view THROUGH the front camera of the phone she is holding, so the hand holding it cannot appear in its own frame, and neither can the phone. NO HAND, NO FINGERS, NO ARM, NO ELBOW, NO PHONE, NO PHONE CASE, NO MIRROR AND NO REFLECTION anywhere in either panel. Both her shoulders sit naturally and neither is raised.

Everything that says selfie is therefore in the CAMERA, not in her limbs:
  * THE LENS IS CLOSE AND WIDE. The phone is barely more than an arm's length away, so the wide front lens exaggerates whatever is nearest it - her nose and chin read slightly large, her forehead looms a little, her ears and the sides of her head fall away fast, and the room stretches out behind her.
  * THE ANGLE IS NOT EYE LEVEL. The camera is a little above her eyeline and looking slightly down at it, so her forehead reads large and her chin recedes.
  * HER EYES ARE ON THE SCREEN, NOT THE LENS. She is watching her own face while she takes it, so her gaze sits slightly below and to one side of the camera rather than meeting it.
  * IT IS BADLY FRAMED. The horizon is a few degrees off, she is not centred, her head sits too high or too low, and there is dead space on one side and none on the other.
  * IT IS A PHONE FILE, NOT A PHOTOGRAPH. Focus is imperfect, there is visible digital noise in the shadows, the indoor white balance is wrong in the ordinary way a phone gets it wrong, and the bright areas clip.
  * SHE IS AT HOME AND NOTHING IS ARRANGED. An ordinary lived-in room behind her, softly out of focus.

SHE IS A WHITE EUROPEAN WOMAN of about forty-eight, AND SHE IS AN ORDINARY PERSON RATHER THAN A MODEL. Cast her the way a real woman that age looks, not the way an advertisement casts: mid-brown hair with a scatter of greys showing at the parting, pulled back into a low untidy ponytail, a square face with a broad jaw, heavy unshaped brows, green eyes, and sun-freckled cheeks with an irregular patch of pigmentation on one cheekbone. Her under-eye shadows are noticeable and her skin looks tired. Her features are asymmetric - one eye sits slightly lower than the other, her nose is not quite straight, and the two sides of her face do not match. She wears no makeup at all, her brows are natural and unshaped, and her hair is unstyled. Nothing about her is glamorous, and neither picture makes any attempt to flatter her.

SHE IS IN HER FORTIES, AND THAT GOVERNS WHAT HER SKIN CAN HONESTLY LOOK LIKE. Her expression lines are ESTABLISHED - they stay put when her face is at rest and they hold a real shadow - but they are not the deep set folds of a woman in her sixties, and she has no heavy jowls and no slack neck. A few greys at the parting are right; a full head of grey is not. Get this wrong in either direction and it is the wrong woman for the age given.

WHAT THE COMPARISON IS ABOUT, AND THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the lines on her face is the same in both panels and NOT ONE OF THEM HAS DISAPPEARED. Her freckles, moles and blemish marks are all still there in the same places. What has changed between the two occasions is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier or better groomed - the same ordinary face is simply less finely etched.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AND UNFLATTERED. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open and obvious across the nose and inner cheeks, finer at the temples and jaw - with several individual pores larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side to the other. Fine pale vellus hairs catch the light along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is greasy and light-catching across the nose and forehead and drier at the outer cheeks. No makeup on either day, so her lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour and her under-eye shadows are her own.

ON THE EARLIER DAY, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are established and plainly visible with her face at rest: a fan of four creases at the outer corner of each eye, three horizontal lines across the forehead, a pair of short vertical creases between the brows, and a line beginning to run down from each side of the nose. Under the hard overhead light each one holds a clear shadow along its length.

ON THE LATER DAY, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Each is about HALF as finely etched - softer, holding a thinner and lighter shadow. The fan at each eye corner is still plainly visible. Her freckles, acne marks and under-eye shadows are exactly as they were.

A snapshot off a phone, not a photograph - slightly soft, slightly noisy, honest and completely unretouched.
